title: Why you flinch before your brain sees danger
hook: Your body reacts to danger before your brain even knows it is there.

narration.text: Your body reacts to danger before your brain even knows it is there.
A tiny part of your brain, the amygdala, acts as a fast warning system.
It can spot threats and trigger a physical response almost instantly.
This happens before the visual information reaches your conscious brain.
So, you might pull your hand away from something hot before you feel pain.
It is an ancient survival mechanism, keeping us safe from immediate threats.
This quick reaction saves vital milliseconds in dangerous situations.
Have you ever noticed your body reacting before you consciously registered danger?

description: Discover the incredible speed of your brain's defence system. Learn how your body reacts to danger before your conscious mind even registers it, thanks to a primitive but powerful part of your brain. This natural survival mechanism keeps us safe every day.
topic: why we flinch before we consciously see danger
